cues.title: First Watch
cues.subtitle: Campaign 1: The Lantern Road  -  Level 1  -  5 Emberfall 1047 AK
cues.text: Three days ago they were strangers in a frontier inn. Tonight, after a goblin raid, a stolen lantern-core, a pack of wolves and a goblin camp, four tired people carry three dead lantern-cores into a hollow in Thornpike Woods: Brannoc the soldier, Ilsevel the archivist and her owl Pell, Tamsin the card player, and Oriel the priestess. Somebody has to keep watch.
Thornpike Woods  -  The Hollow  -  Night
A hollow south of the fork, after midnight. An old ring of stones becomes a fire. The three dead cores sleep in Brannoc's cloak.
Two ways in. One way out, if it comes to it. Good enough.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Our first fire, the four of us. Someone should say something.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Something. There. Can we eat now?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Ilsevel scrapes the moss from a squat old stone at the edge of the hollow and leans close to the carving.

roll.purpose: c2: Read a moss-eaten carving on a stone older than the road, by firelight, from what she remembers of the Hall's road a

cues.text: A Lamplighter way-marker. Here is the Order's sign, and here the old miles. This stone marked the road before the Lantern Road was laid.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: The road moved. The stone stayed.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Stones do.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Three cores. Three villages somewhere with a dark road tonight, and no idea why.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Then we take them back. What's done with a dead one?
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Technically, a core is rekindled at a temple altar, by a Lamplighter of the second rank. I am of the fourth.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Professor, is that a long way of saying you can't?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: It is a long way of saying I have never been allowed to try.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Father Tobin's altar has never once gone out. Would it do?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: I do not know. That is the honest answer. I would like to find out.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Tamsin sits down with her back against the old stone.
At her throat, the plain iron key on its cord begins to hum: one low note, felt more than heard.
Nobody else looks up. Tamsin closes her hand around the key, gets up, and moves to the far side of the fire without a word.
Tamsin? You've gone pale.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Smoke in my eyes, Sunshine. Wrong side of the fire.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Thornpike Woods  -  The Notebook  -  Night
Later. Oriel sleeps. Brannoc keeps the edge of the hollow.
Ilsevel sits upright, notebook open on her knees, in the half-waking trance elves have instead of sleep.
Tamsin has never been able to leave a closed book alone, any more than a locked box.

roll.purpose: c1: Lift a notebook from the lap of an elf in trance, who is resting, not asleep, and still half aware of the world.

cues.text: The notebook leaves Ilsevel's knees the way a leaf leaves a branch. Ilsevel does not stir.
'T.M. Velvet thread; lies about it. Practised hands.' Fair, Professor. Fair.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: 'Gave the boy a honey cake when she thought no one was looking.'
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Tamsin reads that line twice. Then she slides the notebook back exactly as it was, with a sprig of heather between the pages.
Thornpike Woods  -  First Watch  -  Night
First watch. Brannoc sits at the edge of the firelight with his shield across his knees.
I can't sleep. May I sit?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Log's big enough.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Two ways in.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: You said. Twice.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Counting helps.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Helps with what?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: ...Counting.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: In the firelight Oriel sees it: under the grey paint on his shield, the faint raised outline of an anvil.
His thumb is tracing it, and he doesn't know he's doing it.
There's something under the paint.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Old paint.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: All right.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Oriel sits as close to the fire as she can get without burning, and never once turns her back on the dark.
You don't like the dark.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: I sleep with a candle. A priestess of the Lantern-Bearer, twenty-five years old, and I sleep with a candle.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Brannoc unhooks the small lantern from his pack, lights it from the fire, and sets it down beside her bedroll.
I see in the dark. You keep it.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Brannoc...
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Don't thank me. Just sleep.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Oriel lies down beside the lantern and hums the dusk hymn under her breath until she falls asleep. Badly. Brannoc doesn't mind.
Somewhere past the fourth hour, the pines go grey, then gold. The lantern is still burning beside Oriel when she wakes.
Big Man. Did you sleep at all?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Some.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: He gave the last watch to the owl.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Pell says he was excellent at it. Pell says nothing happened at all, which is the point of a watch.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Next time: Back to Brindle Cross, and an old priest's story.
